questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was crucial for me that it was a destination where people spoke English well. Furthermore it was important that the University itself was easy to communicate with and that the website was easy to navigate on so that everything would go smoothly on the administrative and practical parts.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Everything was well informed in the E-mail and people were on site to help you. It was really easy to follow the signs and guidance from staff.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Student helpers greeted you and helped you with filling out the lease and find your room.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student housing - a room round 15 square meters with own bath and fridge. Shared kitchen where you needed to buy your own kitchen supplies.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A shared kitchen with a stove and a microwave.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That you need to buy or bring the kitchen supplies yourself and that they will need to buy a duvet of some sort.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's a shame that there's no oven and they have quite the liberty since they can enter your room when you are not there to do check ups (although it didn't happen often).

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was through their student portal Oasis and it was very to select and change courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International Relations Office could provide guidance or do it for you.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. After the start I found out that I wanted some other courses and I got these as well.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is super easy but be aware that you must make sure that the schedule matches afterwards and there may be some courses you can't take because they are at the same time and they only make 1 class so you can't find the same course at another time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was a lot of work. You have to hand in assignments during the semester in all courses with will constitute half (or less) of your grade. Therefore it is also busy during the semester and not just in the end when you have exams. You also need to attend all classes to understand and pass since there are no books in most of the courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style is very different. It is only professors who teach and not practitioners. Furthermore it is much more reflective content than at home. It is also not case based like back home but more general.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: EU Criminal Policy, EU Competition Law, EU Banking and Capital Market Law, EU Law and ICT, European and International Biodiversity Law, Cybercrime, Technology and Surveillance.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: European Law and ICT, Air and Space Law, EU Economic Law

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Since you are not allowed to bring laptops to the exam you have to print out all your notes which costs money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Croceries

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Every kind of sport. ESN arranged some games but you could also pay a fee to join all sorts of sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Volley because it's an extremely popular sport there and when the weather is nice a lot of people meet to play beach volley and there you can also meet locals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other cities close to Gent like Brugges, Leuven, Antwerpen and Brussels. It's also super cheap with either train or flixbus to go to adjacent countries like Luxembourg, France and The Netherlands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very similar but way more relaxed.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use the buddy you are assigned to and sign up for sports.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some say that Belgiums are even more reserved which seem true but it is possible to find nice Belgium friends as well.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nightlife

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Try and get a room at the University's campus. It seemed as if the people who stayed there had a better time because they naturally met more people. 
2. Go visit other cities and countries it's such a nice opportunity. 
3. Be prepared for the fact that you have to hand in assignments during the semester and do them in good time so that everything doesn't clash at the same time.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It came as a shock to me that exams are written in hand and that you are not allowed to bring your laptop.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Having 6 exams in 20 days but it is duable

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
